requirements.requirement: Record sudo-invoked commands on node1 in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: The validated sudoers configuration directs sudo to the dedicated log with year-bearing timestamps. Pre- and post-restart tests directly show entries containing the invoking user “antrieb,” timestamp, target user, and exact command.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system logs.
requirements.summary: Sudo syslog output was disabled, and unique test-command markers were absent from syslog, auth.log, and messages both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before and after the work and restart. The existing sudo 1.6.8p12 accepted the configuration, and live logging worked without an OS, kernel, or package upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and syslog service, configuration, retained audit data, and new sudo logging were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The functional probes demonstrate representative sudo commands rather than exhaustively exercising every possible sudo invocation form; the validated global sudoers default provides supporting coverage for the broader “every command” wording.
Legacy Ubuntu lacks systemd, so lifecycle failed-service collection was unsupported; recovered syslog health was instead directly demonstrated by its running process.
Final evidence did not explicitly re-list /etc/sudoers.pre-command-logging, although its creation and the absence of any later removal command indicate it was retained.
No cluster state applies to this single-node task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were closely connected to the task: safely validated sudoers replacement, protected log creation, compatible rotation, bounded functional tests, and the required restart protocol. The failed use of unsupported sudo -n is not penalized because no resulting mutation is evidenced. One minor residue is the retained /etc/sudoers.pre-command-logging backup: creating it supported safe rollback, but no cleanup was captured after success, so its continued retention is unnecessary residue. Temporary staging files were absent in the final lifecycle snapshot. No package damage, new listening sockets, or other lifecycle regressions were observed.
